newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Mol, TVK drives Hungary's BUX.
newsitem.headline: Mol, TVK drives Hungary's BUX.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed firmer on Wednesday, bolstered by strong gains in the market's two heavy-weight issues and also helped by the Dow's gain on Tuesday, traders and analysts aid.
The BUX index finished at 5,567.90 points, up 61.38.
Heavily traded oil company MOL and chemicals TVK led the market further up to positive territory with buys of which traders said were linked to positive outlook.
"As for TVK, everybody expects strong a first quarter earnings," said Robert Stalmayer of AB-Moneta Kft.
Not only TVK's after-tax profits were seen strong due to a five billion forint extra revenue from the privatisation agency but also on operating level, he added.
MOL ended at 3,105 forints, up 45; TVK at 2,515, up 50.
Market watchers said MOL's price was up on hopes that its subscription price in its upcoming share offer will exceed 3,000 forints.
Some details of MOL's upcoming privatisation are expected to be released on Wednesday or Thursday.
Analysts said the Dow's rally on Tuesday was also driving the market up.
"The Hungarian market is very significantly correlated to the American market, it's question of liquidity only," said Rudi Voros, analyst at ICE Securities in London.
"We feel there are still shares on the (Hungarian) market which are still not fully priced," he said. This group included OTP Bank which closed at 4,160, up 10.

Voros added, however, that the Hungarian market may go its own way even if the Dow falls because "return could be higher than on mature markets." Earnings reports also can drive the market independently from foreign markets, he said.
Elsewhere on the market the pharmaceuticals stocks strengthened but they had calm trading.
"The pharmaceuticals sector lost the market leading role it played last year...this role is taken over by the chemicals," Stalmayer said.
Egis closed at 10,900 forints, up 300, while Richter at 11,700, up 50. Human stayed steady at 2,950.
The market's newcomer Gardenia continued its rally to a new record of 2,220 forints, before retreating to close at 2,100, up 120. The share, on the market since Monday, was issued at 1,465.
